why: A reconnect now resolves its own login before it logs in: after the connection's `ssh -G` (the scope check, as before) the app asks a second `ssh.configuration`, of the `-f -N` login it is about to run (the login sheet's or, for an automatic attempt, the silent one's, with a placeholder control path), and compares the two apart from Dispatch's own options (`SSHResolvedConnection`), because `Match sessiontype none` or a Match on the command can send that master to another host or account. A recording of a reconnect made before holds one configuration query where the app now asks two; a rewrite cannot add a record. These are the tests whose recordings hold a reconnect login (the scan behind 0022); none is in the corpus now (0022 and 0023 retired them), so this only keeps a recording made with the old code from replaying against the new one. Helper channels gain `-o SendEnv=NAME` only for a connection whose ssh -G sends variables (every test fixture uses -F /dev/null, so none), and saved SSH shells gain a `directory` only for logins captured from now on: neither changes a recorded input.
